blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus was passing through Jericho on his way to Jerusalem. Crowds lined the road to see him.

verses.text: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchæus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchæus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Zacchaeus was the chief of the tax collectors, and he was rich. The people of Jericho did not think well of him. As the story goes on, we hear what the crowd called him.

verses.text: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.

verses.text: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Picture a grown man, a wealthy official, running ahead of the crowd and climbing a tree like a boy. He did not care how it looked. He wanted to see Jesus.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then Jesus came to that place, stopped, and looked up.

verses.text: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus called him by name. Out of that whole crowd, he picked the one person most of them would have passed by. And he did not just say hello. He invited himself to dinner. Today I must abide at thy house.

verses.text: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.

verses.text: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The crowd grumbled. To them, Zacchaeus was a sinner, and a good teacher should not eat with him. But Jesus was not worried about what the crowd thought.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Something happened in Zacchaeus when Jesus called his name and came to his house. Nobody in the story tells him what to do next. He stood up on his own.

verses.text: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord;

segments.speaker: zacchaeus
segments.text: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Half of everything to the poor. Four times back to anyone he had cheated. That is not a small apology. It is a turned-around life. Grace came first, and the change followed.

verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

verses.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Zacchaeus went looking for Jesus, but the story shows that Jesus was looking for him too. A short man in a sycamore tree, disliked by his whole town, was seen, called by name and welcomed.

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 19:1-10; grace before change; no prosperity reading of his giving.

cultural.note: His height and his town's contempt told without mockery.

qa.rewritten: Pastor pass: removed outside claims about Roman tax practice; kept to what Jericho said in verse 7.
